title: Canonical User JWT boundary for tenant activation and resolution surfaces

phases.objective: Require the shared fail-closed User JWT verifier before active-membership rebinding on every tenant activation, operational-attention, resolution, repair, approval, dynamic-detail, and run-archive route while leaving Admin routes unchanged.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Tenant activation and resolution HTTP routes
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Every tenant route is authenticated by the shared User JWT middleware with no fallback secret before tenant and role are rebound from active database membership; missing verifier configuration fails closed and Admin routes remain unchanged.
steps: Authenticate the tenant request through createUserJwtMiddleware before route-local membership resolution.
Fail with verifier-unavailable semantics when JWT_SECRET is not configured instead of accepting a repository fallback secret.
Restrict token verification to the canonical HS256 algorithm contract.
Resolve the caller tenant and tenant role from active membership plus active tenant state rather than trusting token role claims.
Apply the composed canonical-auth then membership guard to every /tenant/ activation and resolution route, including task-source repair and skill-approval mutations.
Keep Admin activation routes and their backend API-key guard unchanged.
Ratchet activationAwarenessRoutes.js into the hardened User JWT governance file set.
assertions: activationAwarenessRoutes.js contains no jsonwebtoken import, local token verifier, or development fallback secret.
All /tenant/ routes compose requireCanonicalUserJwt before requireTenantUserJwt.
A bearer token cannot be verified when JWT_SECRET is missing and the canonical verifier pins HS256.
Membership database authority supplies tenant_id and tenant_role after canonical authentication.
The hardened-file governance scanner permanently covers activationAwarenessRoutes.js.
No repair, approval, provider, database, Production, secret, or external-send side effect is introduced by this auth-only change.
